identity.real_world_identity_notes: Customer GT4 racing car on the AMG GT platform with the 4.0 litre V8 biturbo. Unlike the dual-clutch GT4 cars it uses a purpose-built sequential six-speed racing gearbox in transaxle configuration on the rear axle, pneumatically operated through steering wheel paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
No throttle lift is required on upshifts and no manual blip on downshifts, because the drive detected automatic cut and automatic blip.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mercedes-amg-gt4.20260813t170808566z-d8a41f12 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is established by a registered manufacturer source.

notes: Observed live in ACC 21257365 via guided verification observation acc.mercedes-amg-gt4-2016.20260823t042303819z-65014ec0 by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: ACC's AMG GT4 would not pull away without physical clutch input with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
ACC accepted the guided full-throttle clutchless upshift while the authentic real-car throttle-lift claim remains open.

confidence.basis: Mercedes-AMG establishes the GT4 identity and six-speed sequential transmission. ACC reported the exact model and GT4 class with stable internal id `mercedes_amg_gt4`; the guided drive directly established simulator behavior and cockpit.

claims.basis: The registered manufacturer source establishes the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
Mercedes-AMG specifies a pneumatically operated sequential six-speed racing gearbox in a rear transaxle; the live drive confirmed six paddle gears and clutch-free move-off.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

Telemetry name `Mercedes AMG GT4 2016`, internal id `mercedes_amg_gt4`, and class `GT4` identify the AMG GT4 already curated from manufacturer evidence. The ACC suffix is retained as a simulator identity label while the curated year records the 2018 customer-racing debut.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: Whether the car needs a throttle lift on upshifts is not established. A guided drive settles it, by holding the throttle through an upshift and seeing whether the gear engages.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
